item.title: Federal Council grants start-ups flexibility in working hours
item.description: New special rules adopted on October 28, 2026 Effective date set for December 1, 2026 Targeted exemptions for certain start-up employees The review.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - New special rules adopted on October 28, 2026 - Entry into force set for December 1st, 2026 - Targeted exemptions for certain start-up employees - The revision implements the objective of initiative 16.442
## Key facts - Decision → Federal Council, meeting of October 28, 2026 - Scope → start-ups and some of their employees - Ordinance → revision of OLL 2 - Conditions → specific expertise, autonomy, capital and limited projects - Entry into force → December 1, 2026
On October 28, 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council adopted new special rules for start-ups and some of their employees. The measure aims to ensure greater flexibility in organizing working hours. The press release specifies that the rules were negotiated with the social partners and that they will enter into force on December 1, 2026.
### The revision process
The measure takes concrete form in the revision of Ordinance 2 concerning the Labour Act (OLL 2). During the examination of the preliminary draft of parliamentary initiative 16.442, the National Council’s Economic Affairs and Taxation Committee (EATC-N) had asked the Federal Council to implement the latter by means of an ordinance. The revision of OLL 2 achieves this objective.
The press release describes a targeted derogation, not an indiscriminate amendment. The text refers to derogations from the general rules on working hours and rest periods, subject to compliance with various conditions. The workers concerned must be employed by a start-up, have specific expertise, enjoy broad autonomy in their work and benefit from a plan for participation in the company’s capital. The source adds an additional requirement: the work must concern specific projects of limited duration.
The text stems from discussions held with the social partners in round tables and received a positive reception in the public consultation. The amendment will enter into force on December 1, 2026 and will be incorporated into OLL 2, the ordinance that provides special provisions for certain categories of companies and workers. ## What changes in terms of the rules
The clearest relationship contained in the press release is between the general rule and the exception provided for a defined group. On the one hand, the starting point indicated by the text is the general rules relating to working and rest periods; on the other, the amendment to OLL 2 introduces targeted exemptions for workers who meet the stated requirements. The source does not quantify the hours concerned and does not describe a new standard duration: instead, it documents the principle of flexibility and the conditions for applying it.
### Company, worker and project
The comparison can be viewed on three levels, all present in the text:
| Level | Element indicated by the source | |---|---| | Company | start-up | | Worker | specific skills, broad autonomy and a plan for participation in the company's capital | | Project | activities on specific projects of limited duration |
This breakdown makes clear that being part of a start-up, on its own, does not exhaust the requirements described in the press release. The measure is also linked to the worker's professional characteristics and the temporary nature of the project. In the source's description, this distinguishes the new provision from a general extension of the special rules to all companies or all employees.
For the Swiss labor market, the link stated by the source is direct but limited: start-ups create jobs and, through innovative ideas, contribute to Switzerland's economic development; the revision addresses how working hours are organized for some of their employees. The press release does not provide any additional employment figures for the amendment and does not measure the economic effect of the flexibility.
The text therefore links the stated economic role of start-ups with a targeted change to the rules on working hours, without providing a quantification of the impact. The role of CET-N is also defined precisely: the commission invited the Federal Council to implement the objective of parliamentary initiative 16.442 at the ordinance level. The announced decision therefore concerns the revision of OLL 2 and the organization of working hours. ## Consultation and official documents
The genesis of the provision was accompanied by discussions with the social partners. The press release states that the new provision was developed through roundtable discussions and that the public consultation received it favorably. This element documents the preparatory process, but does not report detailed positions of the participants or attribute statements to individual organizations. The text provided therefore contains no separate quotations or assessments from the social partners.
### What is published together with the decision
The news item refers to three documents. The first is Ordinance 2 concerning the Employment Act, which contains special provisions for certain categories of companies and workers. The second is a commentary on the revision of OLL 2, focusing on the rules of Article 32c for workers at young companies who hold stakes in their own company. The third is the report on the results of the consultation procedure concerning the same revision.
The titles refer to the link between the amendment to the ordinance, holdings in the company and the consultation stage; the text of the news item, however, does not summarize their analytical content. To define the scope of the available information, the press release does not indicate how many start-ups or workers may fall under the provision. Nor does it specify the concrete form of the equity participation plan, or define which skills are considered specific or how broad autonomy is assessed.
These elements cannot be supplemented with examples or estimates not present in the source. The operational detail established without ambiguity remains the date of entry into force: December 1, 2026. The press release describes a rule adopted by the Federal Council and published on October 28, 2026, but does not document any other timelines, sector-specific applications or subsequent results. The measure is therefore presented as a targeted amendment to OLL 2, with explicit conditions and no additional figures on its employment impact.
*Source: [seco.admin.ch](https://www.seco.admin.ch/it/newnsb/Iud3ocFMTVQE)*

item.title: Population alert: 165,4 mln for modernization
item.description: The Federal Council is requesting 165,4 million francs.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Council is requesting 165,4 million francs. - Alertswiss will be maintained and enhanced. - The sirens will be transferred entirely to the cantons. - Cell broadcast will complement the existing alert system.
## Key facts - Decision → message adopted by the Federal Council - Requested credit → 165,4 million francs - Sirens → management and financing transferred to the cantons - Alertswiss → app and website operational since 2018 - New activation system → planned by 2035 - Total costs → 220,9 million up to 2035
165,4 million francs. This is the credit the Federal Council is requesting from Parliament to modernize the population warning system. The message, adopted at today's meeting in Bern, also proposes amending federal law and transferring responsibility for sirens, including the related funding, to the cantons.
According to the Executive's announcement, the reform aims to provide the population with information, warnings and alerts in the event of an incident, using modern channels. The approach is that of a multichannel strategy, designed to provide comprehensive information in crisis situations and take advantage of the widespread use of smartphones. The Federal Office for Civil Protection, referred to by the acronym UFPP, manages the necessary systems.
### Alertswiss and the new siren system
The Alertswiss app and website, operational since 2018, are to be maintained and enhanced, with priority given to accessibility and the availability of important information on smartphones even when there is no network connection. Communications should also be offered in standardized formats so that they can be integrated by third-party providers.
As regards sirens, the transfer concerns both fixed and mobile installations. Responsibility and financing would be transferred entirely to the cantons. According to the proposal, the measure is intended to clarify the division of responsibilities. The Confederation would instead retain responsibility for ensuring the uniformity and security of the remote activation system and would be expected to provide a new one by 2035. ## The comparison between the credit and spending through 2035
The message distinguishes the credit requested from Parliament from the cost framework indicated by the Confederation. The difference does not concern two versions of the same figure: the first amount is presented as a commitment credit for investments, whereas the second comprises investment and operating costs intended to maintain and develop the information, alert and warning systems.
### Three quantities to be read separately
| Item | Amount | Scope indicated | |---|---:|---| | Commitment credit requested from Parliament | 165,4 million francs | Investments | | Costs projected through 2035 | 220,9 million francs | Investment and operations | | Arithmetic difference | 55,5 million francs | Calculation based on the two amounts |
The difference of 55,5 million results from subtracting 165,4 from 220,9. It is a calculation based on the reported values, not a new expenditure item announced by the Federal Council. The text does not provide any further breakdown among the individual components, nor does it assign a specific amount to the cantons.
The scope of the 220,9 million includes the central system, the siren activation system and the development of Alertswiss. The 165,4 million credit, on the other hand, is the one Parliament is being asked to grant to finance investments. For this reason, the figures should be read together but not conflated: one describes the financing requested for investments, while the other describes the overall investment and operating cost through 2035.
Also in terms of channels, the proposal does not describe a straightforward replacement. Alertswiss, with its app and website operational since 2018, is maintained and enhanced. Cell broadcast is introduced to complement and strengthen the existing system, sending short messages to all mobile phones present in the affected area. Fixed and mobile sirens remain part of the system, but responsibilities and funding are transferred to the cantons. The multichannel strategy thus connects tools already in operation, a new mobile-phone channel and the siren infrastructure, while the Confederation retains the task specified for remote activation. ## The timeline and limits indicated in the message
The text from the Federal Council provides some fixed points, but not a complete implementation timeline. The most precise date concerns the remote activation system for the sirens: the Confederation will continue to guarantee its uniformity and security and will provide a new one by 2035. The same year delimits the period under consideration: through 2035, investment and operating expenses are estimated at 220,9 million francs.
### Consensus concerns cell broadcast
For the mobile phone alert system, the source reports that cell broadcast received unanimous support during the consultation. It adds that its launch was brought forward thanks to a separate commitment credit. The text, however, does not indicate the amount of this credit, nor does it describe a service activation date. The consensus cited therefore concerns this specific element; it is not presented as a unanimous outcome for the entire package.
Regarding the transfer of sirens, the proposal indicates where responsibility would lie: the Cantons would take over full responsibility for the management and financing of fixed and mobile sirens. However, it does not indicate the precise timing of the transfer, the distribution of costs among the individual Cantons, or the number of systems involved. The source also does not specify which third-party providers will integrate the standardized communication formats, or in what sequence the Alertswiss app and website will be enhanced.
Parliament remains the addressee of the request to amend the Federal Act and grant the credit of 165,4 million francs. The source does not report a date for parliamentary consideration, final approval, or entry into force. The objective, the multichannel architecture, the new cantonal responsibility for sirens, and the financial framework through 2035 are therefore documented; the operational details for each territory or each channel are not yet. For the population, the message defines how the dissemination of alerts could be strengthened, without indicating individual procedures or instructions linked to a specific event.

item.title: Six new measures to contain costs in the healthcare sector
item.description: Six new measures will start in 2027 The fifth roundtable met in Bern on October 26, 2026 The package concerns outpatient clinics, emergency
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Six new measures will take effect in 2027 - The fifth round table met in Bern on October 26, 2026 - The package concerns outpatient clinics, emergency rooms and home care - The electronic inbox collected approximately 7400 contributions
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | Date | October 26, 2026 | | Location | Bern | | Decision | Six new cost-saving measures | | Effective date | Starting in 2027 | | Previous package | 12 measures decided in 2025 | | Submissions to the inbox | Around 7400 | | Proposals received | Over 15 000 | | Potentially effective and innovative proposals | Just over 500 |
On October 26, 2026, in Bern, the fifth round table on containing costs in the healthcare sector decided to implement six new measures. The body had been established by Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider in November 2024.
### The decision taken in Bern
The round table meets twice a year and brings together representatives of the cantons, referred to in the press release as the CDS, physicians represented by the FMH, hospitals represented by H+, health insurers united in prio.swiss and the pharmaceutical industry represented by scienceindustries. Patient organizations, the scientific community and the Price Supervisor also participate.
The six measures decided concern different areas of healthcare. The first line of action aims to promote the transfer of services to the outpatient sector. The second aims to relieve pressure on emergency departments. The development of care programs for people with chronic illnesses is also planned.
The other measures concern the remuneration of medical devices, with the aim of increasing transparency, and the coordination of medicine supplies for retirement and nursing homes. The sixth measure concerns the promotion of home care.
The partners decided to implement the new package starting in 2027. The decision follows an initial series of 12 targeted measures adopted in 2025. Some of the new measures draw on proposals submitted by the public through an email inbox.
The press release presents the initiative as an intervention in several key areas of the healthcare sector. For the first time, the round table’s work also draws on suggestions collected through an online form open to proposals for reducing the costs of mandatory health insurance. The decision remains with the round-table partners, who reviewed the suggestions received and selected those considered relevant and practically feasible. ## From the targeted package to systemic measures
The comparison between the two rounds of measures shows a difference stated in the communiqué: the 2025 package comprised 12 targeted measures, whereas the six decisions to be implemented from 2027 are defined as being more systemic in nature.
| Element | 2025 package | New measures | |---|---|---| | Number | 12 measures | 6 measures | | Approach | Targeted | More systemic | | Start | Decided in 2025 | Implementation from 2027 |
This distinction has a direct consequence for how the savings are presented. For the new measures, no specific savings potential was quantified, precisely because the interventions are more systemic in scope. However, the communiqué adds a precise condition: if the measures achieve the expected results, the savings potential should be greater than that of the first catalogue.
This is a conditional assessment, not a forecast with a figure. The source does not indicate an overall amount, nor does it translate the six measures into a specific reduction in premiums or individual bills. For those who regard healthcare expenditure as a component of the cost of living, the economic impact therefore remains to be measured.
The electronic mailbox concerned the costs of compulsory health insurance for medical care, referred to in the communiqué by the acronym AOMS. In the Swiss context, compulsory health insurance for residents is governed by LAMal/KVG. However, the text of the decision does not quantify the effect of the new measures on the expenditure of individual insured persons.
### Collaboration as an operational mechanism
The common feature of the six decisions is closer collaboration among the stakeholders. In the measure concerning home care, specialist medical societies should draw up a list of therapies that can preferably be carried out at home. Based on this list, insurers will be able to actively inform patients about the available options.
In homes for the elderly and nursing homes, the agreement instead concerns coordination among doctors, pharmacists and nursing staff. According to the communiqué, the aim is to improve the quality of care and reduce polypharmacy.
A third example concerns medical devices: service providers and insurers have agreed that, from now on, invoices must contain more detailed information about the devices actually used. Greater price transparency should also improve the application of economically appropriate prices. In all these cases, the measure described is not a new amount charged to the patient, but an agreement on information, coordination and the way care is provided. ## Implementation and new direction
The round table also examined the progress of the package decided on in 2025. The assessment communicated to participants is generally positive, but not uniform: overall, most measures can be implemented as planned or with limited delays.
### The outstanding issue concerning digital invoices
The only measure regarding which new differences of opinion emerged concerns the promotion of digital invoices. The differences could not be resolved during implementation. Consequently, the projected savings from this measure cannot be achieved in the short or medium term.
The statement also urges caution regarding the overall figures. For all measures decided, the resulting actual savings cannot yet be estimated precisely, because data for 2026 are not yet available for most measures. The source therefore distinguishes between the expected potential of the new measures and the savings that can actually be measured.
The round table will also change its work schedule. The members agreed to continue their collaboration, focusing more closely on systemic measures. The group of experts will have to prepare a work programme that will no longer aim to adopt a new catalogue of measures every year.
The body will also be called upon to perform an advisory function regarding any cost-containment projects launched by the Federal Council. Its tasks will also include monitoring the implementation of measures already decided. The statement thus describes a shift from an annual sequence of catalogues to coordination and monitoring activities.
### The contribution of the electronic mailbox
The electronic mailbox was a trilingual online form that allowed anyone interested to submit anonymous proposals from May 15 to June 20, 2025. According to the report published by MIS Trend, the initiative received approximately 7400 contributions. These contributions gave rise to more than 15 000 proposals, just over 500 of which were identified by MIS Trend as potentially effective and innovative.
The ideas were forwarded to the group of experts for review. Following internal discussions, those considered relevant and practically feasible contributed to the development of various measures adopted on October 26, 2026. The proposals concerned, among other topics, outpatient care, transparency regarding medical devices, coordination of the supply of medicines to nursing and care homes, and easing congestion in emergency departments.
All proposals submitted via the mailbox will be published anonymously on the website of the Federal Office of Public Health. For an overview of compulsory health insurance in Switzerland: LAMal/KVG e cassa malati.

The first package referred to in the source comprises 12 decisions from 2025; the fifth roundtable adopted six new measures. | Element | Referenced package | New measures | |---|---|---| | Number | 12 decisions in 2025 | six | | Approach | first package | more systemic | | Economic impact | estimated at more than 300 million annually at the time | not estimated |
The 300-million annual threshold is therefore a conditional reference: the savings would have to exceed it if the new measures work. It is not a figure attributed to individual interventions and does not make it possible to calculate what share would relate to outpatient care, programs for chronically ill patients or the other areas.

The most concrete connection concerns how the stakeholders should collaborate. The medical societies will draw up a list of therapies to be carried out primarily at home. This sequence links a professional decision, information for patients and invoice transparency, without quantifying savings for each step. The indicated timetable remains general: the measures will be implemented from next year, without a more precise date in the text. The economic description also has an explicit limitation. The impact of the six measures has not been estimated, so the reference to 300 million annually cannot be turned into a final accounting, savings already available, or an amount allocated to a canton, a hospital, or a category of patients.
### What is documented
The source details two operational steps. Medical societies will prepare a list of therapies to be carried out as a priority at home, and insurers will be able to use it to inform patients. Invoices will have to contain more detailed information on the medical devices used. However, the text does not indicate the number of therapies that will be included in the list, the date of its publication, or the savings associated with these steps.
The text also lacks separate volumes, prices, and timelines for the coordinated procurement of medicines in nursing homes. The comparison with the 12 measures decided in 2025 does not provide a ranking of effectiveness: the source does not indicate which of the six interventions would produce the greatest savings and does not report results already measured for the previous package.
Thus, the content of the decisions and their economic assessment remain separate. The areas of intervention and the collaborative process among medical societies, insurers, and patients are defined; the overall impact has not yet been quantified. ## TL;DR - Fishing falls under services regulated at cantonal level. - Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be officially verified. - The material does not provide fees or seasons for Zurich. - Responsibility may lie with the canton, municipality or institution.
## Key facts - Scope → fishing permit in the Canton of Zurich - Checks → licences, any courses or exams - Calendar → periods and seasons - Territory → authorised waters - Costs → fees and amounts - Competence → competent cantonal authority
Fishing licences appear, in the available information base, among the services that may depend on the canton, municipality or competent institution. This is the starting point for interpreting the request concerning a fishing permit in the Canton of Zurich: the source defines the scope of the verification, but does not provide a fee schedule, a seasonal calendar or a list of waters.
### What the verification includes
The editorial request is divided into several elements. The first is the licence: it is necessary to understand which authorisation is envisaged for the activity in question. The second concerns the requirements, including the possible presence of a course or examination. The wording is decisive: the material refers to courses or examinations that may be required; it does not establish that they are always compulsory.
The other sections concern fishing periods, seasons, authorised waters, fees and the competent authority. These are all elements consistent with a cantonal procedure, but the reference text does not associate them with dates, figures, the names of lakes or rivers, or an identified office of the Canton of Zurich. Adding these details would mean going beyond the available information.
The documentable result is therefore a precise outline of the type of information to seek, not a list of local rules presented as already verified. For fishing licences, the rule indicated by the source is to check requirements, deadlines and amounts against the canton’s official source. The same indication applies to the other services that the information base places within the cantonal sphere.
The request directly concerns anyone who wants to fish in the Canton of Zurich, but its practical content must remain anchored to the data actually available. The text does not attribute a fee, season or specific procedure to Zurich. For this reason, the article can explain how the verification is structured without turning a field to be checked into an undocumented fact. ## The competent level changes the type of response
The most useful comparison starts with a distinction between the issue of the licence and the level that must provide the answer. The information base places hunting and fishing licences among the services that may depend on the canton, municipality or competent institution. The same set includes vehicle registration and inspection, public establishments, university tuition fees and integration programs.
These areas are not juxtaposed to change the subject, but because they show the criterion indicated for cantonal services: requirements, deadlines and amounts must be verified against the canton’s official source. Fishing therefore follows the same documentary pattern. The fact that the question concerns a licence does not, by itself, make it possible to derive the price; a reference to a season does not provide a date; an indication of a competent authority does not necessarily identify a specific office.
| Item | Interpretation permitted by the source | |---|---| | Fishing and hunting licences | May depend on the canton, municipality or competent institution | | Requirements | Must be verified against the canton’s official source | | Deadlines | Must be verified against the canton’s official source | | Amounts and fees | Must be verified against the canton’s official source | | Other cantonal services | Follow rules and offices that must be verified with the competent authority |
### From category to concrete verification
The table separates elements that are often presented together, but that have different functions. The licence identifies the subject of the application. Requirements describe what may be requested to obtain it. Deadlines concern the time of application or validity. Amounts concern the cost. The authority, on the other hand, indicates the entity to refer to.
For the Canton of Zurich, the available source confirms the level of the issue, not the content of each field. This distinction makes the relationship between the keyword and the general rule on cantonal services clear. The keyword asks for requirements and seasons; the editorial angle adds courses or exams, authorized waters, fees and authorities. The verified information base makes it possible to list these dimensions, but not to fill them with absent local data.
The comparison with the other services cited by the source thus produces a concrete result: the answer must be constructed for each individual canton and for each individual administrative responsibility, keeping requirements, calendar, territory and costs separate. This is not a difference in style, but the correct way to avoid confusing a general rule about jurisdiction with a specific requirement for fishing. ## The limitations of the data available on Zurich
An operational answer regarding the fishing permit in the Canton of Zurich should clarify, within the same framework, the type of license, any courses or examinations, fishing periods, authorized waters, fees, deadlines, and the competent authority. These are the elements indicated by the editorial topic. However, the material provided does not associate concrete values relating to Zurich with these items.
### What cannot be added
For fees, the source establishes the criterion of verifying the amounts with the canton’s official source, but does not provide a figure. It is therefore not possible to indicate a cost in francs without introducing data external to the text. The same applies to deadlines: they are mentioned as information to be verified, but are not accompanied by a specific deadline.
The seasonal aspect is similarly limited. The topic refers to periods and seasons, but the information base does not provide an opening date, a closing date, or a calendar applicable to the waters of the Canton of Zurich. Nor does it contain the names of lakes, rivers, or other authorized waters. The correct answer can therefore explain that the fishing area is an item to be checked, but cannot provide a list that is not present.
The same caution applies to courses and examinations. The editorial angle presents them as potentially required; the text states neither a general obligation nor an exemption. It is not possible to turn this wording into a certain condition for every license.
Finally, the source does not identify the name of the Zurich cantonal authority responsible for the matter. Instead, it indicates that fishing licenses may depend on the canton, municipality, or competent institution, and that requirements, deadlines, and amounts must be checked against the canton’s official source. This is the documented relationship between the topic and administrative responsibility.
The resulting framework is therefore practical precisely because it distinguishes what is verified from what is unavailable: the fishing permit is treated as a service potentially regulated at cantonal level; the canton’s official source is the indicated reference for completing the requirements, deadlines, and amounts; no fee, season, water, or specific authority is attributed to Zurich without data present in the material.

item.title: Inflation at 1% in September 2026, national premiums 4.4%
item.description: In 2025, inflation in Switzerland was 0,2%, while in September 2026 it reached 1% year on year.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In 2025, inflation was 0,2% - In September 2026, it reached 1% annually - In December 2025, the index stood at 106,9 points - 2026 premiums: 4,4% in Switzerland, 7,1% in Ticino
## Key facts - National Consumer Price Index → 106,9 points - Index base in December 2020 → 100 - Overall increase in the index → 6,9% - National premiums, actual growth → 4,3% - Housing and mobility indicator in Ticino → 3%
In 2025, inflation in Switzerland was 0,2%, while in September 2026 it reached 1% year on year. In international comparison, similar figures may appear moderate. The source nevertheless compares them with expenses that recur every month: rent, health insurance, taxes, fuel, food and bills.
### The accumulated price level
The annual figure alone does not convey the full trajectory of prices. Starting from 100 points in December 2020, the National Consumer Price Index reached 106,9 in December 2025: the overall increase was 6,9%. Slower inflation indicates that prices are rising less quickly, not that they have automatically returned to their initial levels.
In 2026, forecasts indicated average growth in compulsory health insurance premiums of 4,4% in Switzerland and 7,1% in Ticino, the highest cantonal figure in the country. Subsequent surveys by the Federal Office of Public Health then put the actual national average growth at 4,3%, reducing it slightly.
The distinction between the announced figure and the subsequent one concerns the national average: the 7,1% referring to Ticino is the figure announced for the canton. The LAMal/KVG premium item thus remains an expense that is difficult to reduce in the household budget. ## Housing and mobility: the comparison that changes the interpretation
In the year-on-year comparison for August 2026, Comparis reported a 2,4% increase in Switzerland for the index dedicated to housing and mobility costs. Overall inflation for the same month, however, was 0,8%, a difference of 1,6 percentage points calculated on the same annual basis.
### Basket components
In Ticino, the same indicator stood at 3%. The cantonal figure was therefore 0,6 percentage points higher than the national 2,4%. The comparison shows that housing- and mobility-related components can develop differently across the cantons, meaning that no single national index describes every household budget in the same way.
During the same period, petrol rose by 15,8% and diesel by 23,3%; vehicle insurance and repairs also increased. For an average Swiss family, the Comparis estimate amounted to approximately 1’066 francs in additional annual housing and mobility expenses, or nearly 89 francs per month.
This figure is not presented as an amount applicable to every household. It is an estimate based on a specific basket, which includes items such as rent, ancillary costs, electricity, heating, transport, car maintenance, insurance and fuel. The cost of living therefore also varies depending on the composition of the expenses considered.
The comparison between Switzerland and Ticino makes the gap between overall inflation and some actual expenses easier to see. However, it does not turn the cantonal 3%, nor the additional costs estimated by Comparis, into an automatically applicable measure for every family. ## When the statistical average does not match the bill
Official inflation reflects average price increases, but does not indicate how much more expensive living has become for each individual household. The gap can be considerable when the budget is affected by items that follow a different trend from the national average.
### Premiums and statistical methodology
In calculating the national consumer price index, compulsory health insurance premiums are not counted directly as insurance premiums. The index applies precise criteria and separately records the evolution of healthcare service prices. The methodological distinction is legitimate; for the household budget, however, the premium remains a bill to be paid, regardless of the classification.
For this reason, UST/BFS also publishes specific indicators on premium trends. General inflation data alone do not make it possible to assess the impact of this expense on disposable income. The same applies to housing and mobility, when rent, heating, fuel or repairs affect a household's basket to a different extent.
The source also cites taxes among the expenses that affect financial pressure, but does not provide a breakdown between direct federal tax, cantonal and municipal taxes, or VAT. Nor does it quantify the weight of each item for a specific household. The available material therefore makes it possible to compare national indicators, Ticino data and declared baskets, but not to calculate the individual cost increase for every household.
The difference between a statistical average and a concrete bill remains the central point of the comparison on the cost of living in Switzerland. To explore the topic further, consult cost of living in Switzerland.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/rubriche/ospite/1958944/inflazione-prezzi-indice-premi-nazionale-puo-famiglia-abitazione-rincaro-svizzera)*

item.title: 455 security breach reports in Switzerland in 2026
item.description: BERN — During 2026, the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) has already received 455 reports of data-security breaches
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 455 reports of breaches in 2026 - 343 reports throughout 2025 - Federal investigation into an external IT provider - Possible extension to federal entities and pension funds
## Key facts - Reports 2026: 455 - Reports 2025: 343 throughout the year - Authority: FDPIC, Adrian Lobsiger - Investigation: launched last week - Current focus: external IT provider
BERN — During 2026, the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) has already received 455 reports of data-security breaches in Switzerland. Adrian Lobsiger stated this in an interview with Sonntagsblick.
The comparison given in the source is with the 343 reports recorded throughout 2025. However, the text specifies that the actual number of incidents would be significantly higher because a large number of cases go unreported. The 455 reports therefore represent what reached the authority, not the total number of incidents that occurred.
### The investigation into pension funds
After a cyberattack on a company that provides software to several Swiss pension funds, the FDPIC opened a formal investigation last week. The proceedings currently concern the external IT provider. Lobsiger did not rule out that it could later be extended to federal institutions and pension funds.
The source distinguishes between the data already collected and the investigation that is still open. The extension is not described as a decision that has been made, but as a possibility not ruled out by the Commissioner. For reasons related to investigative secrecy, Lobsiger was unable to provide further details about the specific case.
### The issue of data management
Beyond the specific incident, the FDPIC warned that linking data and removing barriers between silos can increase the risk of data-security breaches. The authority indicated two precautions: transmit only the data that are strictly necessary and preferably work with anonymized test data.
This statement does not attribute a breach to the provider and does not identify the cause of the attack on the pension funds. Instead, it links the risk to the way data are interconnected, transmitted and used in testing. The source does not say which of these elements are present in the case examined by the FDPIC; the connection therefore remains a general warning, not a finding in the proceedings. ## The comparison enabled by the data
The number of reports requires precise interpretation, because the two time bases do not coincide. In 2025, the count covers the entire year; for 2026, the source says that 455 reports had already been received during the year. The 2026 total has therefore exceeded that of 2025, but the text does not present the two figures as equivalent periods.
| Period | Basis indicated by the source | Reports | |---|---|---:| | 2025 | Entire year | 343 | | 2026 | During 2026, already received | 455 | | Calculated difference | 455 minus 343 | 112 |
The arithmetic difference is 112 reports. Relative to the 343 for all of 2025, this amounts to approximately 33%. This is a calculation based on the reported figures, not a percentage announced by the IFPDT. It does not make it possible to turn the figure into a forecast for the end of 2026, because the source does not specify what portion of the year is covered by the 455 reports.
### An increase not to be overinterpreted
There is also a second limitation. The IFPDT points out that many cases are not reported and that the actual number of incidents would be significantly higher. Reports are therefore a measure of incidents communicated to the authority; the text does not provide the number of cases left out of the count. It is therefore not possible to derive the total number of breaches from the 455 and 343 alone, nor to determine how much underreporting weighs in the comparison between the two periods.
This distinction also avoids an undocumented causal link. The source presents the increase in reports and the attack on the pension funds' software provider in the same context, but it does not state that this incident is included in the 455, that it caused the 2025 figure to be exceeded, or that it explains a specific share of the increase.
### Two different levels
The first element is therefore aggregate: reports received by the IFPDT in Switzerland. The second is specific: a formal investigation launched after an attack against a software provider for several pension funds. The verifiable relationship between the two is only the one indicated by the text: the second fact led to the opening of the investigation, while the first describes the volume of reports. Separating the two levels makes it possible to read the figures without turning them into an explanation of the specific case. ## Digital threat and responsibility still to be clarified
In the interview, Lobsiger described the threat posed by artificial intelligence as “real.” In the same passage, however, he distinguished the technological threat from the analysis of causes: in the vast majority of reported attacks, he stated, the weak point is not technology but human error.
The two statements describe different aspects. The first is an assessment of the threat posed by artificial intelligence; the second concerns what emerges from the analysis of the causes of attacks already reported. The source does not say that artificial intelligence was used in the attack on the pension fund provider. Nor does it say that, in that case, the weak point was human error. Attributing either cause to the proceedings currently underway would go beyond the available information.
### The investigation phase
The situation regarding responsibility also remains open. For now, the formal investigation is directed against the external IT provider. Lobsiger did not rule out extending it to federal bodies and pension funds, but the text does not present this possibility as a decision already adopted. Investigative secrecy also prevents further details about the specific case from being known.
The source does not indicate what data were involved, how many pension funds were affected, or what the outcome of the attack was. It does not report the outcome of the investigation or any sanctions. These omissions make it impossible to measure the concrete impact of the incident and do not justify identifying responsible parties beyond the current scope of the proceedings.
### What is established
Three elements remain verifiable. The first is the volume of reports submitted to the IFPDT and the fact that the actual number of cases is considered higher because of the presence of unreported cases. The second is the opening of a federal investigation following an attack on a software provider for several Swiss pension funds. The third is the warning from the IFPDT about the greater exposure associated with interconnected data, together with its preference for anonymized test data.
These elements create a national picture of data security, but not a complete reconstruction of the attack. The statistical data, the general assessment of artificial intelligence, the human error identified in the majority of reported cases, and the responsibility still under investigation remain separate. This separation, more than the numbers taken in isolation, defines what the source currently allows us to state.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/attualita/1958918/dati-violazioni-sicurezza-aumento-svizzera)*

item.title: Referendum on the law requiring a collective labor agreement
item.description: This distinction is relevant for reading the text without conflating the two matters: the formal success of the referendum against the amendment
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - October 23, 2026: referendum formally successful - 66 006 valid signatures out of 66 574 submitted - The cantonal referendum was not validated - Eight cantons were required for validation
## Key facts - Publication → 23 October 2026 - Contested amendment → 19 June 2026 - Submission of signatures → 7 October 2026 - Signatures submitted → 66 574 - Valid signatures → 66 006 - Cantons cited → Neuchâtel and Ticino - Cantonal threshold → eight cantons
The referendum committee had submitted 66 574 signatures on 7 October 2026. The Federal Chancellery determined that 66 006 of the submitted signatures were valid. The source directly links this verification to the conclusion that the referendum was formally successful. In this passage, therefore, the communiqué reports an outcome of the signature verification and not a result at the ballot box.
### Two outcomes indicated separately
The same communiqué also addresses the cantonal referendum. It specifies that it was also supported by the cantons of Neuchâtel and Ticino, but that the required minimum number of eight cantons was not reached. For the cantonal referendum, the stated outcome is therefore failure to validate it.
This distinction is relevant for reading the text without conflating the two matters: the formal success of the referendum against the amendment to the federal law and the failure to validate the cantonal referendum are reported as two different outcomes. The source does not add a decision on the merits of minimum wages, the collective employment agreement or the legislative amendment. ## The comparison between the available figures
The communiqué allows for a limited numerical comparison, because the two figures refer to the same collection of signatures on October 7, 2026. The total submitted is 66 574, while the number recognized as valid is 66 006. The difference is 568 signatures: 66 574 − 66 006 = 568. This is a calculation derived from the source values, not an additional figure attributed to the Federal Chancellery. The source does not explain the reasons for the discrepancy.
| Item | Value | Reference | |---|---:|---| | Signatures submitted | 66 574 | submission of October 7, 2026 | | Valid signatures | 66 006 | finding of the Federal Chancellery | | Arithmetic discrepancy | 568 | 66 574 − 66 006 |
### What the comparison measures
The comparison measures the gap between the signatures submitted by the referendum committee and those recognized as valid. It does not measure the extent of support beyond the submission, indicate participation in a future consultation, or anticipate the outcome of a vote. The text does not provide an official percentage either. Therefore, the figures can describe the formal step already communicated, but they do not make it possible to quantify an effect on wages or collective agreements.
The link with the content of the law is defined solely by the designation of the amendment: granting generally binding force to the collective labour agreement and minimum wages lower than the cantonal minimum wages. The communiqué does not specify amounts, occupational categories, sectors, or an entry-into-force date.
### The eight-canton threshold
At cantonal level, the text names Neuchâtel and Ticino as cantons that supported the cantonal referendum and indicates eight cantons as the required minimum. It does not state how many cantons supported it overall. It is therefore not correct to turn the two names cited into a total or derive from them a numerical distance from the threshold. The only stated outcome is that the minimum was not reached. Thus, the data on signatures, which leads to the formal success of the referendum against the federal amendment, and the data on the cantons, which leads to the failure to validate the cantonal referendum, remain separate. ## Scope of the news
The available timeline establishes three stages: the amendment is dated June 19, 2026, the referendum committee submitted the signatures on October 7, 2026, and the statement was published on October 23, 2026. These dates make it possible to reconstruct the sequence of the events reported, but they do not add any subsequent schedule. The text does not give a date for a vote or indicate the next institutional step.
### The informational limitations of the statement
The source does not report statements by the referendum committee, positions on the content of the law, or reasons for the validity of the individual signatures. Nor does it explain why the discrepancy between 66 574 deposited signatures and 66 006 valid signatures is of that size. Regarding the cantonal referendum, it indicates that the threshold of eight Cantons was not reached, but does not publish the total number of supporting Cantons.
The text does not quantify the minimum wage or the minimum wages concerned, identify the collective agreements involved, or describe effects on employers or workers. The wording concerning minimum wages lower than cantonal minimum wages defines the subject of the amendment, but does not document an increase, reduction, or suspension of wages. Similarly, the stated support of the Cantons of Neuchâtel and Ticino is not presented as a change to their wage rules.
### What can be stated
Based on the statement, it can be stated that the referendum against the amendment to federal law achieved formal success after the signatures were verified and that the cantonal referendum was not validated because the minimum of eight Cantons was not reached. However, the source cannot be attributed with a finding on the merits of the law, a voting date, or an already measured impact on the minimum wage. The documented scope remains the procedural and institutional one indicated by the Federal Chancellery.
*Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/-t2rtlvDYznI)*

item.title: EPFL and ETH among Europe’s top 20 universities for patents filed
item.description: In last year's European ranking, the Federal Polytechnic Institute of Lausanne (EPFL) totaled 107 patent filings and ranked 12th.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - EPFL: 107 patent filings in Europe last year - ETH Zurich: 101 patent filings and 16th place in Europe - Switzerland ranks fourth in Europe with 463 spin-offs - 57,5% of Swiss spin-offs are growing
## Key facts - Data source: European Patent Office (EPO) - Survey: 2025 data - Scope: over 800 departments examined - EPFL: 107 deposits and 12th place in Europe - ETH Zurich: 101 deposits and 16th European place - Swiss spin-offs: 463 - Growth phase: 57.5% of Swiss spin-offs - Towards markets with new requests: 18.1% of Swiss spin-offs
In last year's European ranking, the Federal Polytechnic Institute of Lausanne (EPFL) totaled 107 patent filings and ranked 12th. The Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH Zurich) recorded 101, taking 16th place. The two universities are therefore among the top 20 European universities in terms of number of deposits.
The report is based on 2025 data published by the European Patent Office. In the statement released on Wednesday, the EPO explained that it had examined, for the first time, more than 800 departments belonging to universities and scientific institutes that aim to commercialize the results of their research.
### Switzerland's position
The same survey places Switzerland in fourth place in Europe for patent filings from 463 spin-offs. The source defines these entities as entities detached from an institution, dedicated to the development of an innovative product or service. The data broadens the reading beyond the two polytechnics and shows the presence of structures created around research.
57.5% of Swiss spin-offs are still in the growth phase. 18.1% of the total instead concerns those that have already passed this stage and are orienting themselves towards the markets through new requests for financing. The press release presents the two percentages as distinct indicators of the development phase.
According to the EPO, Europe is a place of excellence for cutting-edge research. The ability to transform this innovative force into new technologies and businesses, adds the statement, is of growing importance for the competitiveness of the Old Continent. For Switzerland, the data therefore presents together the position of the polytechnics in the European ranking and the consistency of the spin-offs surveyed. The numerical comparison between the two federal institutes of technology makes it possible to read the ranking without confusing positions and volumes. EPFL has six more patent filings than ETH Zurich: 107 versus 101. The two results are four positions apart: 12th and 16th. The available text does not report the complete ranking, so the comparison remains limited to the data explicitly stated.
### The numbers for Swiss universities
| Institution | Reported figure | |---|---| | EPFL | 107 patent filings, 12th place in Europe | | ETH Zurich | 101 patent filings, 16th place in Europe | | University of Zurich | 55 patent applications | | University of Bern | 27 patent applications | | University of Basel | 23 patent applications |
Adding the two values for the institutes of technology gives 208 patent filings. The three values reported for the other Swiss institutions, on the other hand, amount to 105 patent applications: 55 plus 27 plus 23. The arithmetic difference is therefore 103 units. The calculation uses only the numbers published for last year; it does not amount to a new ranking, because the source refers to the institutes of technology using the term European-level patent filings and to the other universities using the term patent applications.
The sectors indicated also help distinguish the profiles. At EPFL, most innovations concern medical technology, biotechnology and measuring instruments. For ETH Zurich, the main patent fields are biotechnology, medical technology and information technology. Biotechnology and medical technology therefore appear for both, while measuring instruments are associated with EPFL and information technology with ETH Zurich. The press release does not quantify patent filings by individual sector: the comparison describes the main fields, not their numerical weight. The text does not indicate how many patent filings belong to each category, nor does it relate the sectors to the positions in the ranking. For this reason, the comparison should be read as a map of the stated specializations, not as an internal ranking of the sectors. The transition from patents to spin-offs makes it possible to examine research also from an entrepreneurial perspective. The press release records 463 spin-offs in Switzerland: 24 have exceeded the threshold of a valuation of 500 million dollars and have expanded internationally. In addition, 89 of these companies have been acquired by larger companies.
### What the data show and what they do not show
The breakdown proposed by the EPO distinguishes young companies still in the growth phase from those that, having passed that stage, set out for markets with new funding requests. The percentages indicated in the source — 57,5% for the first group and 18,1% for the second — therefore describe two different stages. However, the text does not provide a sum of the shares, nor does it clarify whether the classifications are completely separate; therefore, the entire distribution of spin-offs cannot be reconstructed from those values alone.
The scope of the EPO's 2025 data is defined: for the first time, the survey examined more than 800 departments belonging to universities and scientific institutes, focused on bringing the results of their research to market. The available text does not list all 20 European universities or the total number of filings for each. For Switzerland, EPFL and ETH Zurich are highlighted, while the other figures reported concern the patent applications of the Universities of Zurich, Bern and Basel. A complete breakdown by sector and individual spin-off is missing. The picture therefore makes it possible to examine the documented results, but does not authorize predictions about future developments.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/info/svizzera/EPFL-ed-ETH-tra-le-20-universit%C3%A0-europee-per-brevetti-depositati--4181978.html)*

item.title: Zenith: around 100 jobs at risk in Le Locle and another 100 abroad
item.description: Around 100 of Zenith's approximately 200 jobs in Le Locle, canton Neuchâtel, would be at risk.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - About 100 jobs at risk in Le Locle - Another 100 jobs could be cut abroad - Zenith is consulting staff about possible collective redundancies - The strategy focuses on high-end watchmaking
## Key facts - Brand → Zenith - Swiss office → Le Locle (NE) - Property → LVMH, French luxury group - Employment in Le Locle → approximately 200 employees - Places at risk in Le Locle → around 100 - Places at risk abroad → another 100 in the distribution network - Strategy → greater concentration on high-end watchmaking - Factors cited → strong franc, US customs duties and international geopolitical tensions
Around 100 of Zenith's approximately 200 jobs in Le Locle, canton Neuchâtel, would be at risk. The estimate concerns the Swiss headquarters of the brand and comes from internal sources cited by the AWP agency. For the distribution network abroad, the same sources indicate another 100 positions potentially affected.
The data is part of the personnel consultation procedure launched by the company, which could result in a collective dismissal. The news, published by the newspaper Le Temps, was confirmed by a company spokesperson. The confirmation concerns the start of the consultation; the figures attributed to internal sources instead indicate positions at risk, while collective dismissal remains a hypothesis.
Zenith is a watch brand from Le Locle (NE) and belongs to the French luxury giant LVMH, Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton. The geographical distribution of the estimate is therefore double: one part concerns the Le Locle headquarters, the other the foreign network. The source does not indicate which countries or which structures abroad would be involved, therefore the reference remains to the distribution network as a whole.
### The reorganization indicated
According to internal sources, the direction indicated for the company is to adapt production volumes to actual demand and focus the brand more on high-end watches. The same reconstruction reports that, in the period following the post-pandemic recovery, the good results of some collections would not have prevented Zenith from accumulating losses from year to year. This report explains why the procedure is described as a reorganization, but does not allow us to quantify either the losses or the timetable of possible cuts. The text also links the operation to a downsizing of industrial and commercial activities, considered excessive compared to current needs. These are elements attributed to internal sources, not a detailed plan with already definitive measures. The comparison of the available figures helps put the announcement in context without confusing the Swiss site with the overall scope of the possible action. At Le Locle, the reference is approximately 100 jobs at risk out of a base of approximately 200 employees. The 100/200 ratio corresponds to approximately 50% of the site's workforce. This is a calculation based on the approximate figures reported by the source, not an official percentage communicated by Zenith.
| Scope | Source figure | Ratio or limitation | | --- | --- | --- | | Le Locle | About 100 jobs at risk out of about 200 employees | About 50% of the local workforce | | Abroad | Another 100 jobs in the distribution network | Total number of employees is missing | | Overall figure indicated | About 200 jobs at risk | Indicative sum of the two blocks |
Abroad, by contrast, another 100 jobs are indicated in the distribution network, but the source does not provide the total number of employees in that network. Therefore, it is not possible to calculate a comparable share for abroad. The overall estimate of about 200 jobs at risk should be read as an indicative sum of about 100 jobs in Le Locle and another 100 outside Switzerland. It cannot be used as Zenith's total number of employees, because the figure of about 200 employees refers only to the Le Locle site.
### Volumes, prices and positioning
A second comparison concerns the industrial strategy. For Zenith, the source speaks of a stronger focus on high-end watchmaking and the need to align production with actual demand. For other Swiss watchmakers, the text describes a direction already taken: higher prices accompanied by lower volumes. The two elements should not be conflated: the source does not say that Zenith has already raised prices, nor does it quantify the decline in its volumes. Instead, it says that some collections performed well, while the brand, after the recovery following the pandemic, had reportedly accumulated losses year after year. The comparison therefore distinguishes the strategic choice indicated for Zenith from the industry example cited for other players. It does not, however, provide a common measure for determining how much each component contributed to the jobs indicated. The pressures listed in the source are both market-related and structural. The difficulties include the strong franc, U.S. customs duties and international geopolitical tensions. According to the same account, these factors are compounded by an excessive scale of industrial and commercial activities relative to current needs. The source presents these elements as reasons for the reorganization, but does not attribute a specific share of the losses or jobs at risk to each of them.
The passage on the Swiss sector broadens the picture without turning it into a forecast for Zenith. Bloomberg, cited in the source, observes that raising prices in the presence of lower volumes would benefit exclusively brands such as Rolex, Patek Philippe and Cartier; operators in the mid-range segment and suppliers, by contrast, would be hit hard.
> “This strategy only helps brands such as Rolex, Patek Philippe and Cartier”
The text does not establish that Zenith belongs to one of the categories identified by Bloomberg. Instead, it reports a distinction between the brands that would benefit from higher prices with lower volumes and the mid-range operators or suppliers described as being under pressure. This limitation prevents the comparison from being turned into an automatic classification of the Le Locle brand.
### The limits of the news
The employment data are also limited. Approximately 100 jobs at risk in Le Locle and another 100 abroad are indicated, but there is no breakdown by function, department or country. No timetable for the consultation or outcome of the procedure is indicated. The source does not quantify annual losses and does not describe a final form of the reorganization. The most clearly defined piece of information at the company level is therefore the launch of the consultation; the distribution of the possible cuts and their actual implementation remain expressed in potential terms. For the Swiss labor market, the documented point remains the Le Locle site: the text does not provide a broader total for the Swiss watchmaking sector as a whole and does not allow the estimate to be extended to companies other than Zenith.

item.title: PVL reluctantly recommends a yes to AVS financing
item.description: After a close discussion, the delegates of the Liberal Greens (PVL), meeting in Bern, chose to recommend "yes" to the additional funding of the AVS.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The PVL recommends a yes vote on supplementary AVS funding - Yes also to the fireworks initiative - No to the proposal on marriage discrimination - The four proposals will be voted on November 29
## Key facts - Decision → yes with gritted teeth to the financing of the HSV - Place of the delegates' → meeting in Bern - Glacier → retreat rate of 5% thisyear - Popular → vote consultation on four proposals on 29 November
After a close discussion, the delegates of the Liberal Greens (PVL), meeting in Bern, chose to recommend "yes" to the additional funding of the AVS. The decision was communicated at the end of the meeting and defined as a "yes to gritted teeth". The party linked it to the popular decision on the introduction of the 13th monthly payment, explaining that with this recommendation it intends to assume its responsibility.
The political motivation concerns the way in which the new service is financed. The PVL advocates a moderate increase in value added tax, VAT, to create partial and reliable funding and spread the costs across all shoulders. However, the communiqué does not present this intervention as the solution to all the AVS issues: for the remaining challenges, the party speaks of a sustainable reform.
> "A moderate increase in value added tax (VAT) would make it possible to guarantee a reliable partial financing and to share the costs among everyone. To address the remaining challenges, however, the AVS needs sustainable reform.”
The statement cited by Keystone-ATS attributes the statement to Patrick Hässig, who is part of the National Council's Social Security and Health Commission. The report thus highlights two distinct plans: the financing of the 13th annuity and the call for broader reform for the remaining insurance challenges.
### The other decisions of the meeting
The popular initiative "For a limitation of fireworks" won the support of the PVL after a controversial confrontation. On the proposal that aims to ensure fair taxation for spouses and to end marriage discrimination, however, the position has been clear: the Liberal Greens reject it. The party recalls that the people only approved individual taxation in March and argues that this decision must be respected and applied consistently.
Already in April, the PVL had expressed its support for the amendment of the federal law on war materiel. The people will be called to pronounce on the four proposals on November 29. ## The tax issue: funding and reform do not coincide
The central point is not merely the affirmative vote, but the separation between the source of funding and AVS reform. In the text released after the assembly, the PVL argues that a moderate increase in VAT could provide reliable partial funding. In the same passage, it acknowledges that other challenges remain and links them to the need for sustainable reform. The position, therefore, does not amount to a promise that the entire AVS/AHV pension provision issue has been resolved.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the tax distinction helps interpret the news correctly. The press release refers to value-added tax and does not indicate any measure involving direct federal tax. Nor does it mention cantonal or municipal tax rates. Indeed, verified facts about the Swiss tax system distinguish the AFC/ESTV, which is responsible for IFD and VAT, from cantonal administrations, which administer cantonal and municipal taxation. The reference to the cantons therefore serves to define the scope: the proposal described in the source concerns VAT, whereas it is not presented as a change to local taxes.
### What can and cannot be quantified
| Element | Documented information | |---|---| | Instrument indicated | Moderate increase in VAT | | Stated objective | Reliable partial funding of the 13th pension payment | | Amount of the increase | Not reported in the press release | | Overall reform | Considered necessary to address AVS's remaining challenges |
The table shows the report's main limitation. The tax instrument and its political function are clear, but the new tax rate, the effective date, and the calculation of the burden on individual consumers or households are missing. The statement about spreading the costs across everyone is a PVL justification, not a numerical breakdown.
The text also provides no basis for measuring an effect on the cost of living, nor does it link the proposal to LPP/BVG or other areas of pension provision. It is therefore not possible to derive from the press release alone a change in an individual's pension or an amount to be paid. The only explicit economic detail is the increase in VAT described as “moderate,” without a figure.
The PVL's choice should therefore be understood as a political recommendation on funding the 13th pension payment. The decision does not contain, in the available report, a technical timetable for the sustainable reform called for to address the remaining challenges. ## From social security to the PVL's political agenda
The delegates' assembly also addressed issues that go beyond financing the AHV. In his speech, party president Jürg Grossen referred to climate and energy issues, as well as relations with Europe. He linked the climate issue to the 5% retreat of glaciers recorded this year: according to the Bernese National Councillor, a policy focused exclusively on CO2 is no longer sufficient.
### Climate, water and relations with Europe
In the reasoning attributed to Grossen, the climate issue encompasses water, energy, forests and agriculture, as well as vital resources and, ultimately, well-being. The PVL also stated that it would continue to exert pressure for a national water-storage strategy and a genuine climate policy. The source therefore reports a political line and some declared priorities, but does not indicate an operational plan, spending or a deadline for these initiatives.
The party leadership also reiterated the importance of reliable relations with the European Union. The Bilateral III agreements were described as indispensable for Switzerland. The PVL unanimously supports the agreements as a whole and declares that it is committed to further developing the bilateral approach. On this front too, the report does not describe additional measures or a negotiating timetable.
These issues are not included in the list of the four proposals put to a popular vote on November 29. The amendment to the Federal Act on War Material, by contrast, had already been supported by the PVL in April and is one of the proposals on which the people will vote. The source does not anticipate the outcome of the consultation and does not specify the content of the legislative amendment beyond its subject matter.
The documented picture therefore remains precise but limited: a recommendation on financing the 13th pension payment, two other positions on popular initiatives, support already decided on war material and a political line on climate and Europe. For the pension issue, see AVS and pension.

item.title: 358 confirmed redundancies: first hypothesis 450 jobs
item.description: On Friday morning Sunrise announced in a statement that it will cut 358 jobs.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Sunrise announces 358 layoffs - The first hypothesis indicated 450 jobs - The consultation with Syndicom has ended - Social plan and voluntary exit for some
## Key facts - → Sunrise Company - → Telecommunications sector - Communication → on Friday morning - Dismissals reported → 358 - Reduction assumed last month → 450 jobs
On Friday morning Sunrise announced in a statement that it will cut 358 jobs. The announcement of the layoffs dates back to last month, when a reduction of 450 jobs was expected. The communication therefore updates the number indicated above, but the source does not specify when the cuts will be applied or which locations, departments or professional categories will be affected.
### The operational framework and the measures announced
> Sunrise speaks of a "profound realignment of the operating model".
As part of this realignment, the company claims to have systematically reviewed both contracts with suppliers and external expenditure items. The statement does not go into the substance of the contracts nor does it associate a single item of expenditure with the figure of 358 redundancies.
In the meantime, the consultation with the Syndicom trade union has ended. For those who will lose their jobs, Sunrise indicates a solid social plan. For some employees, it also indicates the possibility of joining a voluntary exit program. The text does not quantify the recipients of these measures and does not specify conditions or deadlines. ## The comparison between the two listings
The change from 450 to 358 should be read as a comparison between two company communications, not as a statistical series on employment levels. The first information, from last month, spoke of a hypothesized reduction; the one released on Friday morning indicates 358 layoffs. The difference between the formulations matters: the source does not present 450 as a figure already confirmed, but as a hypothesis.
| Moment of communication | Data reported | | --- | --- | | Last month | Assumed reduction of 450 jobs | | Friday morning | 358 redundancies announced | | Arithmetic difference | 92 uses |
### Calculation and its limits
The arithmetic difference is 92 uses: 450 minus 358. Compared to the first hypothesis, 92 out of 450 are equivalent to about 20.4%. This percentage only measures how much the figure communicated on Friday is lower than the reduction assumed last month. It does not indicate the trend of other employment data, which the source does not report.
The press release offers an element of operational context: Sunrise talks about a profound realignment of the operating model and reports on the systematic review of contracts with suppliers and external expenditure items. However, it does not clarify which revision led to the change from 450 to 358, nor does it link a specific expenditure item to a certain number of redundancies. The comparison is therefore limited to the two values communicated. ## Measures for those involved
The consultation with Syndicom has ended, and the communiqué accompanies this step with two indications for employees. For those who will lose their jobs, there is a solid social plan. For some employees it is also possible to opt for a voluntary exit program.
The wording separates those who will lose their jobs from employees for whom a voluntary membership is indicated. The source does not clarify whether the two audiences coincide, how many people will be able to access the program or how many will be the recipients of the social plan. It does not indicate the amount or duration of the plan, the deadlines for exit, or the methods by which the employees concerned will be identified.
The implementation schedule of the 358 redundancies and any distribution between locations, departments or categories also remain undocumented. The available text does not say whether the voluntary programme is already open, what the deadline is or how the consultation with Syndicom has changed the measures. The announced measures can therefore be reported, but the individual or operational details cannot be reconstructed from this source.
